packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-11 - unverified first reading (image-only)

Exposure note: my session context (assistant memory index) names the overall fragmentarium project and batch label, but nothing in my context gave a proposed identification or reading for this packet. This is a blind reading.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview, face A)
- Two small parchment fragments on black ground, with colour chart and ruler. Left fragment roughly 9 x 4.5 cm, right fragment roughly 4 x 4 cm (by ruler).
- Orientation: text upright as photographed.
- Both fragments are ruled with red horizontal lines (staff lines, apparently single/multiple red lines) carrying neumes (musical notation) above text lines. This is a notated liturgical chant fragment: alternating text lines and neume lines.
- Left fragment: top line of text partially visible ("..ue bin fate te ..."?), then a red-ruled zone with a modern pencil shelfmark note ("Stams STA, Frg. 23 ..."? modern), then a neume line, then a text line "..to quide planta urte ..."(provisional, to be read from tiles).
- Right fragment: fragmentary, red ruling, a modern pencil note, one text line "..ttea fer.."(provisional).
- No rubrics, initials or glosses visible at overview scale. No columns discernible (fragments too small).

TILE image-002.jpg (left fragment, native detail; whole fragment visible). Crops: crop-01.jpg (text line 1, contrast), crop-02.jpg (text line 2, contrast).
Layout seen here: red ruling; text line at top (y~150), then a four-red-line staff (y~220, 285, 355, 425) carrying dark gothic/square-ish neumes (Hufnagel-type, rhomboid puncta, virgae with tails, a descending series of rhombs at left), then a second text line (y~510), then the top two red lines of a further staff (y~565, 635) with no surviving notes. Modern pencil note between first two red lines: "Stams STA, Frg. 23-1r"(?) - modern, not part of text. Gothic textualis bookhand, syllables spaced for underlay (text set under music, so word division unreliable).

image-002 line 1 (text under/above staff; top edge cropped, ascenders partly lost):
  ] ue(? or uc) biu(? three minims after b: biu / bin / bni) fa t c(? read "fatte"/"facte"; 3rd letter has cross-stroke like t, 4th rounded c/e) te ta[ (or ti[; cut at right edge)
image-002 lines 2-5: red staff lines with neumes only, no text (plus modern pencil shelfmark note).
image-002 line 6 (text):
  ]cto(? first letter cut; "-cto") quide (horizontal stroke over "de" running to the p - possibly macron, i.e. quide(m)? or an extended ascender of round d) planta urte(? or "ui te" / "ut te"; second letter r-like) uin[ (or uim[; cut at right)
image-002 lines 7-8: two red lines of the next staff, no notes surviving.
Unread/limitations: left and right edges torn; line 1 tops of letters partly lost; neumes not transcribed (pitch not readable without clef; no clef visible).

TILE image-003.jpg (right end of left fragment, overlapping image-002; and the whole right fragment). Crops: crop-03.jpg (left fragment, end of text line 2), crop-04.jpg (right fragment text line).
Overlap: the left part of this image repeats the right end of the left fragment (image-002 lines 1-8); not new text except a clearer view of the end of image-002 line 6.
  image-003 line 6 (= image-002 line 6, right end): ]te uine e(? last letter round, c/e, possibly with something after it; "uinee"/"uinea"? not settled) [edge]
  image-003 line 1 (= image-002 line 1, right end): ]te ta[ (second word: t + a, then edge)

Right fragment (image-003, right half):
  Layout: red ruling, lines at y~140/210 (top, slanted, staff), ~275, ~345 (staff lines), text line ~420, red line ~490 (top of next staff). Small neume remnants at top (y~95-215: a few dark notes on the upper staff lines). Modern pencil "Frg. 23-2r"(?) between red lines - modern.
  image-003 right-frag line 1-3: staff with only fragmentary neume tops (not transcribed).
  image-003 right-frag text line (y~420):
    ]mica(? or ]nica / ]tica; first letters damaged and stained; a horizontal stroke above "ca" - possibly abbreviation macron or a neume-line stroke) spe c(? or spe t)[ ... a further letter c/e? before edge
  image-003 right-frag line below: red line, no text.
Limitations: right fragment is very small and stained; first letters of the text line obscured by dark stain.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-004.jpg, overview, face B = other side of the same two fragments, presumably)
- Same two fragments, other face. Left fragment: top text line ("..ndi pepen.."? provisional), modern pencil note, a red four-line staff with neumes and a vertical red stroke (divider/bar line) toward the right, then a text line with a red(-touched) enlarged initial "B" ("..a do re .. mus Beati.."? provisional), then a further staff with neumes at the bottom edge.
- Right fragment: heavily stained; red ruling, faint neumes, faint text traces.

TILE image-005.jpg (face B, left fragment, native detail; whole fragment visible). Crops: crop-05.jpg (text line 1), crop-06.jpg (text line 2).
Layout seen here: text line at top (y~110); four-red-line staff (y~185, 245, 315, 380) with Hufnagel-type neumes (virgae with tails, rhomboid puncta, clivis/pes shapes); a vertical red stroke crossing the staff at x~850 (y~160-375) - a red division/bar line; text line (y~460) with an enlarged initial B touched/struck with red (vertical red stroke through the bow), at x~940; then a further staff (red lines y~525, 600, 650) with neumes on it and no text surviving below. Modern pencil note "STA, Frg. 23-1v"(?) between the first two red lines - modern. At the far left of the upper staff (x~90-250, y~330-380) dark shapes that may be neume groups (looks superficially like "Na"; I take it as notation, not text - uncertain).

image-005 line 1 (top text; tops of letters partly cut):
  ]?ndi (one or two letters before n, only lower parts: possibly u/m minims) pepen[ (second letter could be c; read "pepen") ... then gap/stain ... a single round letter fragment o/e/c at x~790 [edge]
image-005 lines 2-5: staff with neumes; red vertical divider at x~850 after a neume group.
image-005 line 6 (text, syllables spaced under music):
  ]a   do   re   [blank with show-through]   mus   B(red-touched initial)eati(? last letter i/t, cut at edge)[
  (syllables written as: "a" / "do" / "re" / "mus", wide spacing for melismas; "B" is a larger initial with red stroke, starting a new chant item after the red divider)
image-005 lines 7-9: red staff lines with neumes, no text surviving.

FACE B, right fragment: only seen at overview scale (image-004); no detail tile was supplied for it. Heavily stained; red ruling and faint neume and text traces visible; not read. A wider/native tile of the right fragment, face B, is needed.

SUMMARY OF SELECTED SPANS / UNREAD AREAS
- Read: all text lines visible on face A left fragment (2 text lines), face A right fragment (1 text line), face B left fragment (2 text lines).
- Unread: face B right fragment (no detail image); all neumes (no clef visible, pitches not transcribed).
- Material is a notated chant manuscript (gothic textualis, Hufnagel-type neumes on red 4-line staves); only short syllabified text survives, so connected prose of 10+ lines does not exist on these fragments.
- Pencil notes are modern archival foliation, not part of the text.
- Nothing done beyond the brief's rules (I listed the packet directory to get image file names and sizes; I did not open packet.json).
- Did not hit the image limit.
